subject: physiology
title: Iodide Trapping, Thyroid Peroxidase, and Thyroid Hormone Actions

steps.tx: Synthesis of thyroid hormones begins with the active concentration of inorganic iodide from circulating blood plasma into thyroid follicular cells. This uphill transport process is mediated across the basolateral membrane by the **sodium-iodide symporter**, which concentrates iodide thirty- to fifty-fold against its electrochemical gradient.
steps.say: The sodium-iodide symporter actively concentrates circulating iodide into follicular cells using energy from the sodium gradient.

nodes.label: Basolateral Na+/K+-ATPase Creates Downhill Inward Sodium Gradient
Sodium-Iodide Symporter (NIS) Cotransports 2 Na+ Ions with 1 Iodide Ion
Intracellular Iodide Concentrated 30- to 50-Fold Above Systemic Plasma Levels
Apical Anion Transporter Pendrin Translocates Iodide into Follicular Colloid

steps.tx: Once inside the follicular colloid, iodide is oxidized to active iodine and covalently attached to tyrosine residues on thyroglobulin. Both oxidation and organification are catalyzed at the apical membrane by the heme enzyme **thyroid peroxidase**, requiring hydrogen peroxide generated by dual oxidase two.
steps.say: Thyroid peroxidase oxidizes iodide and attaches it to tyrosine residues on thyroglobulin within the colloid.

left.title: Organification Reactions
points: Iodide oxidized to reactive iodinating species via TPO and H2O2
Iodination of tyrosine position 3 yields monoiodotyrosine (MIT)
Subsequent iodination at position 5 yields diiodotyrosine (DIT)
Inhibited pharmacologically by propylthiouracil and methimazole

right.title: Coupling Reactions
points: Catalyzed within thyroglobulin matrix by thyroid peroxidase
Coupling of 1 MIT + 1 DIT forms triiodothyronine (T3)
Coupling of 2 DIT molecules forms thyroxine (T4)
Stored extracellularly in follicular lumen as colloid

steps.tx: Administration of excessive pharmacological doses of inorganic iodide acutely inhibits thyroid peroxidase activity and downregulates the sodium-iodide symporter. Known as the **Wolff-Chaikoff effect**, this temporary autoregulatory shutdown prevents thyrotoxic surges, serving as the physiological basis for administering potassium iodide following nuclear exposure.
steps.say: The Wolff-Chaikoff effect temporarily shuts down thyroid hormone synthesis when exposed to high doses of iodide.

nodes.label: Acute Administration of High Pharmacological Doses of Inorganic Iodide
Inhibition of Thyroid Peroxidase and Suppression of H2O2 Generation
Downregulation of Basolateral NIS mRNA and Membrane Protein Expression
Temporary Block Prevents Thyrotoxicosis; Escape Occurs over 10 to 14 Days

steps.tx: Although the thyroid gland secretes predominantly thyroxine in a twenty-to-one ratio relative to triiodothyronine, thyroxine functions largely as a prohormone. Peripheral activation requires **type 1 iodothyronine deiodinase** in liver and kidneys to remove a five-prime iodine, generating biologically active triiodothyronine.
steps.say: Thyroxine is mainly a prohormone, converted in liver and kidneys into biologically active triiodothyronine by deiodinases.

steps.tx: Over ninety-nine point nine percent of circulating thyroid hormone is transported bound to plasma proteins, predominantly thyroxine-binding globulin. Because only the minute unbound fraction is biologically active, conditions like pregnancy that elevate **thyroxine-binding globulin levels** increase total hormone levels while maintaining normal free thyroxine.
steps.say: Over ninety-nine percent of thyroid hormone is protein-bound; only free hormone is biologically active and regulates TSH.

left.title: Elevated TBG (e.g., Pregnancy, Estrogen)
points: Estrogens increase hepatic synthesis and sialylation of TBG
Increases total circulating T4 and total T3 concentrations
Free T4 and free T3 remain strictly normal (euthyroid state)
Serum TSH remains within normal physiological reference ranges

right.title: Decreased TBG (e.g., Cirrhosis, Nephrotic)
points: Urinary protein loss or hepatic synthetic failure
Decreases total circulating T4 and total T3 concentrations
Free T4 and free T3 remain completely normal
Patient remains clinically euthyroid without symptoms

steps.tx: Inside target tissues, triiodothyronine binds nuclear thyroid hormone receptors, stimulating transcription of sodium-potassium ATPases, uncoupling protein one, and beta-1 adrenergic receptors. This widespread metabolic stimulation produces the **calorigenic effect of thyroid hormones**, increasing basal metabolic rate and whole-body oxygen consumption.
steps.say: Thyroid hormones stimulate sodium pumps and uncoupling proteins to increase basal metabolic rate and heat generation.

vis.alt: Calorigenic action of triiodothyronine inducing sodium-potassium ATPase and uncoupling protein with rising oxygen consumption
vis.caption: Calorigenic action of triiodothyronine inducing sodium-potassium ATPase and uncoupling protein with rising oxygen consumption. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Autoimmune stimulation of thyroid-stimulating hormone receptors by circulating thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulins causes **Grave disease hyperthyroidism**. Unrestrained follicular epithelial proliferation produces a diffuse vascular goiter, severe heat intolerance, progressive weight loss, fine hand tremors, and sinus tachycardia, while retro-orbital fibroblast activation yields exophthalmos.
steps.say: Graves disease is caused by autoantibodies stimulating TSH receptors, producing goiter, heat intolerance, and tachycardia.

vis.caption: Follicular hyperplasia in Graves disease, lymphocytic infiltration, and endocrine thyroid pathology.

steps.tx: Untreated severe congenital hypothyroidism produces the devastating syndrome of **congenital cretinism**. Because thyroid hormones are essential for normal cerebral dendritic branching, axonal myelination, and growth hormone-mediated linear skeletal growth, untreated neonatal deficiency results in irreversible intellectual disability and disproportionate dwarfism.
steps.say: Congenital hypothyroidism causes cretinism with irreversible mental retardation and dwarfism if untreated at birth.

rows: Heat intolerance, tremor, weight loss, goiter
Cold intolerance, weight gain, constipation, dry skin
Umbilical hernia, coarse facies, severe neurocognitive arrest
